about.title: About
paragraphs: I'm Pedro, a QA engineer from Santander. I studied Mathematics at the University of Cantabria and got into software through a Java bootcamp in 2021. They hired me as a QA engineer as soon as it finished, and it suited me.

What I enjoy most is checking that a feature really does what it should, whether by automating the tests or by catching problems early. I'm detail-oriented, I like to get to the bottom of a problem until I understand it, and I use AI tools a lot in my work, carefully.
I write down what I learn in my QA Wiki.

jobs.title: Senior QA Engineer at Alvatross by SATEC
jobs.meta: Telecom OSS transformation for EWE (Germany), on a TM Forum ODA platform
bullets: Design and run tests in Jira + Xray for service-order flows (add, modify, delete, suspend/reactivate) of L2/L3 business services: orchestration through TM Forum APIs, business rules and fallout handling.
Building the API test automation with Karate: scenarios that create service orders and check how each one is decomposed into the expected services.
Built a one-click Postman smoke suite for production deployments, with a baseline/verify mode that flags any response that changed after a release.
Run release regression and pre-production validation, triaging each failure as a product defect or an environment issue and raising bugs from the failing step.

jobs.title: QA Engineer at IriusRisk
bullets: Cut CI pipeline time by 40% at no extra infrastructure cost with a Python optimization model (MILP, PuLP) that balances E2E specs across parallel containers.
Owned the test strategy for the Security Content module, defining the test mix across unit, integration, backend and E2E.
Automated backend API tests in Java with REST Assured and JUnit 5: JSON schema validation, negative cases and Qase integration.
Helped migrate the E2E suite from TestCafe to Playwright with TypeScript, cutting execution time by 80%, and reviewed requirements and designs early (Shift Left).

jobs.title: QA Engineer at Fieldeas
jobs.meta: Hybrid, Santander. Field service management SaaS
bullets: Designed and ran functional, regression and integration tests across several client projects, reporting 500+ bugs prioritized by product risk.
Built and maintained the E2E suites with Cypress and JavaScript, taking the team from manual testing to a scalable automation model.
Validated data with SQL as part of the test cases and coordinated releases with development in Jira.
Trained new team members on tools and automation practices.

items.name: CI Shard Advisor
items.tagline: Optimal parallelization of Cypress suites in CI, without relying on Cypress Cloud.
items.description: Analyzes your Cypress run reports and recommends the spec partition that minimizes total pipeline time, with optimality certified by a branch & bound algorithm. It's the same optimization problem behind the 40% pipeline cut at IriusRisk.
features: Runs in the browser with a demo already loaded; drop in your own reports and they never leave your machine.
Web app, CLI with a quality-gate mode and a local REST API.
Recommendations ready to paste into GitHub Actions or Bitbucket Pipelines.

items.name: Screen Recorder (QA mode)
items.tagline: Chrome extension for reporting bugs with full evidence in a single recording.
items.description: Records your screen, window or tab while capturing what a developer needs to reproduce the bug: console logs synced with the video, uncaught exceptions, network requests as HAR and numbered user steps. No time limits, no watermark, no account.
features: Automatic step recording exportable as *.steps.md, each step with a paste-ready Cypress or Playwright selector. Typed values are never logged.
Files the report directly in Jira Cloud or Linear.
Tested against bench.pedromorago.com, a page I built that breaks on demand, so the capture is checked against known failures.
